name: Free cooling and economisers
applications: Reducing mechanical cooling hours in temperate climates
Water-free cooling where water supply is constrained
principle: An economiser uses outdoor conditions to do the cooling work instead of a compressor. Air-side designs bring outside air in; water-side designs cool the loop with a dry cooler or cooling tower; packaged units combine both. The saving is proportional to annual hours below the switch-over temperature, so the same equipment saves far more in a high-latitude climate than in the tropics - which is exactly the PUE spread the Uptime survey reports.

process_steps.name: Controls compare outdoor and return conditions against the switch-over point
Unit selects mechanical, partial or full economiser operation
Cooling is delivered to the room or loop
Return air or water is rejected and the cycle repeats

performance.metric: unit capacity, Vertiv Liebert DSE free-cooling system
performance.basis: Liebert DSE product page: 50-165 kW standard range with packaged units around 250-400 kW; the unit is water-free, avoiding the makeup water a chilled-water plant needs.

source.note: Vertiv Liebert DSE free-cooling system 50-165 kW product page, read 2026-11-12

performance.basis: Uptime Institute 2025 survey: facilities in high latitudes in North America and Europe have PUEs of 1.3 or better, against a weighted average of 1.54 across respondents; climate, not only design, drives the spread.

source.note: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2025 (31-page report PDF), text extracted and read 2026-11-14

advantages: Large energy saving in climates with cool ambient hours
Water-free options remove the water permit and plume
limitations: Saving collapses in hot humid climates
Air-side designs import pollutants and humidity
Part-load control and switch-over points are the usual commissioning failures
